note: Thresholds and per-row scheduling rules only; never proof text. Scores are estimates, not measurements.

portfolio.note: Competition keeps the standard 6x3 + 22 loop (design section 10: near saturation, compile slots go to weaker rows).

golf.note: Amendment A7: at most 4 screens on the original and 12 per row on candidates (best 8, next 4); no ddmin when T0 > 600. A14: G1/G2 first. rc4: G3s (syntax sugar, about 1 compile per batch) right after G3 on default routes. G4h/G6/G2s are valid names but enabled on no route.

priority.note: No per-row rules: weak_rows stays empty (row lists from earlier runs on the final benchmark are benchmark-specific). Weak sources go first within longest-first order. kernel-decide-tiny rows (no API, about 8 golf compiles each) start first so their gain is locked in while LLM rows are still in preflight; this departs from pure longest-first. Putnam stays last per design section 10; its expected gain over the original is the largest (estimate), so raise competition here if rows risk never starting.

expected_score.note: Estimates calibrated on the team dashboard's per-source means (OpenAI direct runs); not measurements of this harness.
